To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the best performing feature sets for copy-move forgery are the keypoint-based Sift and Surf features, as well as DCT, DFT, KPCA, and Zernikemoments; 2) the best performing algorithmic pipeline is to use Sift features, followed by a robust outlier rejection step, and a matching step that is able to handle outliers; 3) the best performing outlier rejection step is the robust RANSAC-based outlier rejection step,

(i) the Sift feature set performs best in terms of detection performance, (ii) the Zernike feature set is most robust against downsampling, (iii) the PCA feature set is most stable against noise, (iv) the DCT and DWT features exhibit the best robust performance against downsampling and noise, (v) the DCT, DCT+DWT, and DWT feature sets are best suited for the detection of postprocessed copy-move forgeries, and

(1) the Sift feature set is the most robust against noise and downsampling, and the most reliable in identifying copied regions; (2) the DCT feature set is the best at detecting affine-transformed copies; and (3) the Zernike feature set is the fastest to compute.

providing an in-depth analysis of existing copy-move detection methods.
the evaluation and analysis of the most prominent feature sets for copy-move forgery.
providing a thorough analysis of copy-move detection approaches and their performance on real data.

no single feature set outperforms the others in all scenarios, and thus the best approach depends on the application scenario and the expected postprocessing steps.

the best performing feature set is Sift, which achieves a detection rate of 98% on a per-image level and 94% on a per-pixels level, with a very small number of false positives.

the detection of copy-moved content is a very challenging problem, which requires a combination of multiple feature sets.
there is no single best feature set, as the choice of feature set depends strongly on the type of postprocessing applied to the copy.
